title: 70. Numeracy & Number Systems: Least Common Multiple
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the least common multiple by finding the first positive multiple shared by the given integers.
questions.question: What is the least common multiple of \(4\) and \(6\)?
questions.explanation: List positive multiples up to the first common value: \(4\): \(4\), \(8\), \(12\); \(6\): \(6\), \(12\). The smallest value appearing in all lists is \(12\). The alternative \(24\) is a common multiple but is not the smallest positive one.
questions.hint: Compare positive multiples until the first shared value appears.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the least common multiple by finding the first positive multiple shared by the given integers.
questions.question: Two bells ring together at the same time. One bell rings every \(8\) minutes, and the other rings every \(10\) minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: The bells next coincide after the smallest positive common multiple of the two periods. List positive multiples up to the first common value: \(8\): \(8\), \(16\), \(24\), \(32\), \(40\); \(10\): \(10\), \(20\), \(30\), \(40\). The smallest value appearing in all lists is \(40\). The alternative \(20\) is not a common multiple of the two ringing periods.
questions.hint: Compare positive multiples until the first shared value appears.
